prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” roofing company for hurricane-rated replacements — the right choice depends on your exact Miami neighborhood, roof type (shingle, tile, metal), whether it’s residential or commercial, and whether you’re using insurance. I can find and compare top local installers for you if you tell me your ZIP code and whether this is a house or commercial building.

Meanwhile, here’s how to find and pick a top hurricane-rated roofer in Miami plus what to check for:

What to require from any roofer
- Proper licensing and insurance
  - Florida roofing contractor license (verify on the Florida DBPR license lookup).
  - Current general liability and workers’ compensation insurance (ask for certificates).
- Miami‑Dade compliance
  - Use products and methods compliant with Miami‑Dade County HVHZ (high‑velocity hurricane zone) or have Miami‑Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) for the materials used.
  - Installations meeting TAS/UL standards for wind/impact (TAS 201/202/203, UL 2218 for impact, or Class 4 shingles).
- Strong warranties
  - Manufacturer’s warranty on the roofing material plus a workmanship (contractor) warranty. Ask how long each covers and whether the workmanship warranty is transferable.
- Certifications & training
  - Manufacturer-certified installer status (e.g., GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) and FORTIFIED Roof (Insurance Institute/IBHS) credentials are a plus.
- Written contract & scope
  - Detailed contract with scope of work, materials (brand/model/ratings), cleanup plan, permit responsibility, project timeline, payment schedule, and start/finish dates.
- Permits & inspections
  - Roofer should obtain all building permits and schedule inspections. Never let them skip permits.
- References & portfolio
  - Local, recent references and photos of completed hurricane-rated installations.

Where to check reputation
- Florida DBPR license lookup (verify license number)
- Miami‑Dade County contractor/permit records
- Google Reviews, Better Business Bureau, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and local homeowner associations
- Ask for recent local references and go see finished roofs if possible

Red flags
- No license or insurance, or unwillingness to provide proof
- Large up‑front cash-only payments or pressure to sign immediately
- Extremely low bids far below others with vague scope
- No permits or refusal to provide a written contract

Typical next steps I can do for you
- Compile a short list (3–5) of top-rated Miami roofing companies that specialize in hurricane-rated replacement for your ZIP code
- Compare their credentials (licenses, NOAs, manufacturer certifications, warranties) and give pros/cons
- Provide questions and a template to request written estimates

If you want, tell me your ZIP code, whether it’s residential or commercial, roof material, and whether you’ll be using insurance — I’ll find and compare the best local hurricane-rated roof replacement contractors.
